content: Fatty acid desaturase 2 (FADS2) is a gene that encodes the enzyme known as Delta-6 desaturase (D6D). While the enzyme is primarily associated with Delta-6 desaturation activity, it has also been shown to catalyze Delta-8 and Delta-4 desaturation reactions, despite its naming convention. Function FADS2 belongs to the fatty acid desaturase (FADS) gene family. Enzymes in this family are responsible for introducing double bonds at specific positions in the carbon chain of fatty acids, a process known as desaturation. Members of the FADS family are considered fusion proteins, consisting of two main domains: an N-terminal cytochrome b5-like domain and a C-terminal desaturase domain that spans the membrane multiple times. Both domains are characterized by conserved histidine motifs, which are essential for their enzymatic activity. The evolutionary origin of this gene cluster is thought to involve gene duplication, as evidenced by similarities in exon and intron organization. Clinical Significance FADS2 has been implicated in interactions with breastfeeding. Specifically, breastfed children carrying the C allele of the FADS2 gene were reported to have an average of 7 points higher intelligence quotient (IQ) compared to those with the less common G allele. However, this difference diminishes when adjusted for maternal IQ. Attempts to replicate this finding in a study of 5,934 eight-year-old children were unsuccessful. The study found no evidence of a relationship between the common C allele and negative effects of formula feeding. Contrary to the original report, children who were homozygous for the rare GG allele performed worse when formula-fed compared to other formula-fed children. Additionally, a study involving over 700 families found no evidence supporting either a direct or moderating effect of the original single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) (rs174575) on offspring IQ. Furthermore, no effects were observed for two additional FADS2 polymorphisms (rs1535 and rs174583) or for maternal FADS2 status on the IQ of their children.
